Pearl pushed me in that direction immediately.
Gemini and Cancer kept that theory alive for a moment, but summer Solstice still did not quite fit.

Pearl fit once I read it through the answer.

solutionNarrative: I first read Pearl and Gemini and Cancer too literally and drifted toward astrology and holidays. Pearl could be read as "Pearl", while Gemini and Cancer could be read as "June zodiac signs", so the board still felt open instead of solved.

Summer Solstice changed the direction because "June solstice" gave me a testable phrase, not just a loose topic. Once that line worked, I had a fixed place to put the repeated word and could go back through the earlier clues with a clearer target.

I then checked "Pearl", "June zodiac signs", "June named for Juno", and "Father's Day in June". Those checks mattered because each one landed as ordinary wording on its own, so I was not forcing five separate hints into one bag. The board started to behave like one phrase pattern across Pearl, Gemini and Cancer, Summer Solstice, Juno (Roman goddess of marriage), and Father's Day (today in US+UK+...).

That left very little room for the earlier false start. The answer was "Things associated with June", and the last step was simply making sure every clue used that same reading cleanly before treating the solve as finished.
